cues.en: So that's what I've done with my life.
cues.zh: 这就是我这一辈子做的事。

cues.en: As a kid, I grew up on a farm in Florida, and I did what most little kids do. I played little baseball,
cues.zh: 小时候，我在佛罗里达的农场长大，也做大多数小孩会做的事。我打过少年棒球，

cues.en: did a few other things like that.
cues.zh: 还做过一些类似的事。

cues.en: But I always had the sense of being an outsider, and it wasn't until I saw pictures in the magazines and a couple other guys skate,
cues.zh: 但我一直觉得自己是个局外人，直到我在杂志上看到照片，又看到几个人玩滑板，

cues.en: I thought, wow, that's for me, you know, because there was no coach standing directly over you. And these guys, they were just being themselves. There was no opponent directly across from you. And I love that sense. So I started skating when I was about 10 years old in 1977.
cues.zh: 我心想，哇，这就是我要的，因为没有教练直接站在你头上管你。那些家伙就是在做自己。你对面也没有直接对手。我喜欢那种感觉。所以我大概10岁、1977年开始滑板。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: when I did, I picked up pretty quickly. In fact, here's some footage from about 1984.
cues.zh: 我一上手就学得挺快。事实上，这里有一段大概1984年的影像。

cues.en: It wasn't until '79
cues.zh: 直到79年，

cues.en: I won my first amateur championship.
cues.zh: 我赢得了第一个业余冠军。

cues.en: And then by '81,
cues.zh: 然后到81年，

cues.en: I was 14, and I won my first world championship,
cues.zh: 我14岁，赢得了我的第一个世界冠军，

cues.en: which was amazing to me.
cues.zh: 这让我非常惊讶。

cues.en: And in a very real sense, that was the first real victory I had. Watch this. This is a Casper slide with the boards upside down. Mental note on that one.
cues.zh: 而且从很现实的意义上说，那是我第一次真正的胜利。看这个。这是一个板子倒过来的 Casper slide。这个得记一下。

cues.en: And this one here,
cues.zh: 而这一招，

cues.en: an Ollie.
cues.zh: 是 Ollie。

cues.en: So...
cues.zh: 所以……

cues.en: And she mentioned that is overstated
cues.zh: 她提到过，这说法被夸大了

cues.en: for sure,
cues.zh: 确实如此，

cues.en: but that's why they called me the godfather of modern street skating.
cues.zh: 但这就是为什么他们叫我现代街式滑板教父。

cues.en: Here are some images of that.
cues.zh: 这里有一些相关的画面。

cues.en: Now I was about halfway through my pro career
cues.zh: 当时我的职业滑板生涯大概过了一半

cues.en: in,
cues.zh: 具体是在，

cues.en: I would say, what, mid eighties.
cues.zh: 我想想，八十年代中期吧。

cues.en: Freestyle itself, we developed all these flag ground tricks as you saw, but there there was evolving a new kind of skateboarding where guys were taking it to the streets.
cues.zh: 自由式滑板本身，我们发展出了你看到的这些平地动作，但当时也在演化出一种新的滑板方式，大家开始把它带到街头。

cues.en: And they were using that ollie, like I showed you. They were using it to get up on the stuff like bleachers and handrails and over stairwells
cues.zh: 正如我刚才展示的，他们当时在用 ollie 这个动作。他们用它来跳上看台、扶手以及楼梯间之类的障碍物

cues.en: and all kinds of cool stuff.
cues.zh: 以及各种酷炫的东西。

cues.en: So it was evolving upwards. In fact, when someone tells you they're a skater today,
cues.zh: 所以它在不断演进。事实上，现在有人说自己是个滑板手时，

cues.en: they pretty much mean a street skater because freestyle took about five years for it to die.
cues.zh: 他们基本指的是街头滑板手，因为自由式滑板大概花 了五年时间就消亡了。

cues.en: And at that stage, I'd been a champion champion for
cues.zh: 而在那个阶段，我已经蝉联了

cues.en: eleven
cues.zh: 十一年的

cues.en: years,
cues.zh: 冠军，

cues.en: which... And
cues.zh: 这……而且

cues.en: suddenly, it was over for me. That's it. It it was gone. They took my pro model off the shelf, which was essentially pronouncing you dead publicly. That's how you make your money. You know, you have a signature board and wheels and
cues.zh: 突然之间，这一切对我而言都结束了。就这样。它没了。他们把我的签名款滑板下架了，这基本上等于公开宣告你的死讯。你就是靠这个赚钱的。你知道的，你有签名板、轮子、

cues.en: shoes and clothes. I had all that stuff and it's gone.
cues.zh: 鞋子和衣服。我曾经拥有这一切，而现在它们都没了。

cues.en: The crazy thing was there was a really liberating sense about it because I no longer had to protect
cues.zh: 最疯狂的是，这带来了一种真正的解放感，因为我不再需要去捍卫

cues.en: my record as a champion. Champion again, champion sounds so goofy, but it's what it was. Right?
cues.zh: 我作为冠军的纪录了。冠军，再次说起这个词感觉太滑稽了，但事实就是这样。对吧？

cues.en: And I got to what drew me to skateboarding, the freedom was now restored where I could just create things because that's where the joy was for me. Always was creating new stuff.
cues.zh: 而我得以重新找回最初吸引我走向滑板的东西，那种自由现在失而复得，我可以随心所欲地创造，因为那才是我快乐的源泉。我一直都在创造新东西。

cues.en: The other thing that I had was a deep well of tricks to draw from that were rooted in these flat ground tricks. Stuff that the normal guys were doing was very much different. So as humbling and rotten as it was, and believe me, it was rotten. I would go to skate spots,
cues.zh: 我拥有的另一大优势是，我有一套深厚的招式储备可以调用，它们都根植于这些平地技巧。普通人玩的那些东西与此截然不同。所以，尽管这既丢脸又糟糕，相信我，这真的很糟糕。我去那些滑板圣地时，

cues.en: and I was already, like, famous guy. Right? And they... Everyone thought I was good. But in this new terrain, I was horrible.
cues.zh: 我其实已经是个大名人了。对吧？他们……每个人都觉得我很厉害。但在这种新地形上，我烂透了。

cues.en: So people would go, oh, he's...
cues.zh: 所以大家会说，哦，他……

cues.en: Happened to Mullen?
cues.zh: Mullen 怎么了？

cues.en: So humbling as it was, I began again. Here are some tricks that I started to bring to that new terrain.
cues.zh: 虽然很受打击，但我又重新开始了。下面是我开始带入那片新领域的一些技巧。

cues.en: And again, this is undergirding
cues.zh: 再说一次，这是基础

cues.en: layer of influence of freestyle
cues.zh: 自由式影响力的底层

cues.en: that made me... Oh, that one? That's like the hardest thing I've ever done.
cues.zh: 让我……哦，那个？那是我做过最难的事了。

cues.en: Okay. Look at that. It's a dark slide. See how it's sliding on the backside?
cues.zh: 好。看那个。是个暗色滑板。看到它怎么在后侧滑行了吗？

cues.en: Those are super fun and actually not that hard. You know what? The very root of that... See, Casper's...
cues.zh: 那些超级好玩，其实也没那么难。你知道吗？那个的最根本……看，Casper 的……

cues.en: You throw it.
cues.zh: 你把它抛出去。

cues.en: Simple as that. Right? No biggie. And your foot foot, the way it grabs it is is...
cues.zh: 就这么简单。对吧？没什么大不了的。你的脚，它抓住的方式是……

cues.en: I'd seen someone slide on the back of the board like that. I was like, how can I get it over? Because that had not yet been done. And then it dawned on me, here's part of what I'm saying. I had an infrastructure. I had this deep layer where where it's like, oh my gosh. It's just your foot. It's just the way you throw your board over. Just let the ledge do that, and it's easy. And next thing you know, there's 20 more tricks based out of the variations.
cues.zh: 我见过有人那样在板子背面滑行。我就想，我怎么才能翻过去？因为那还没人做到过。然后我恍然大悟，这就是我说的部分内容。我有一个基础设施。我有这个深层，就像，天哪。就是你的脚。就是你抛板的方式。让台沿去做那件事，就很简单了。接下来你知道，基于这些变化就有了 20 多个新招式。

cues.en: So that's the kind of thing that... Here... Check this out. Here's another way, and I won't overdo this. A little indulgent. I understand.
cues.zh: 所以就是那种……这里……看这个。这是另一种方式，我不会过度渲染。有点放纵。我明白。

cues.en: There's something called a Primo slide. It
cues.zh: 有一种叫 Primo slide。它

cues.en: is the funnest trick ever to do.
cues.zh: 是最最好玩的招式。

cues.en: It's like skimboarding.
cues.zh: 就像浅滩滑板。

cues.en: If this one... Look how it slides sideways every which way. Okay. So when you're skating and you take a fall, the board sits that way or that way. It's kind of predictable.
cues.zh: 如果这个……看它怎么向各个方向侧滑。好。所以当你滑板摔倒时，板子会那样或那样放着。有点可预测。

cues.en: This, it goes every which way. It's like a cartoon that falls. And that's what I love the most about it. It's so much fun to do. In fact, when I started doing them, I remember because I got hurt. I had to I had to get a knee surgery. Right? So there were couple of couple of days where... Actually, couple of weeks where I I couldn't skate at all. It would give out on me. And I would watch the guys. I'd go to this warehouse where a lot of guys were skating, my friends.
cues.zh: 这个动作可以向任何方向转。就像卡通片里摔倒那样。而这正是我最喜欢它的地方。做起来特别有意思。其实，我刚起步做这些动作时，我记得自己受了伤。我不得不去做膝盖手术。对吧？所以有几天……实际上，有好几周我完全没法滑板。膝盖会突然撑不住。我就看着其他人滑。我会去那个仓库，很多朋友都在那儿滑板。

cues.en: And I was like, man, I gotta do something new. I wanna do something new. I wanna start fresh. I wanna start fresh. And so the night before my surgery, I'd watch them. I was like, how am I gonna do So I ran up, and I jumped on my board, and I cave in.
cues.zh: 我就想，哥们，我得做点新东西。我想做点新东西。我想重新开始。我想重新开始。所以手术前一晚，我看着他们。我心想，我该怎么做到呢。于是我跑起来，跳上滑板，结果摔了个四脚朝天。

cues.en: And I flipped it down. And I remember thinking, I landed so right footed thinking that if my knee gives, they'll just have more work to do in the morning.
cues.zh: 我把板翻正落下。我记得当时想着，我是右脚先落地，心想万一膝盖撑不住，他们明早手术就得多干点活了。

cues.en: And so when it was the crazy thing, I don't know how many of guys have had surgery,
cues.zh: 所以 crazy 的是，我不知道有多少人做过手术，

cues.en: but
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: you
cues.zh: 你

cues.en: were so helpless. Right? You're on this gurney, and you're watching the ceiling go white. Every time, it's always that. And right when they're putting the mask on you before you go to sleep,
cues.zh: 感觉特别无助。对吧？你躺在推床上，看着天花板变成白色。每次都是这样。就在他们给你戴上口罩、让你入睡之前，

cues.en: all I was thinking is, man, when I wake up and I get better, the first thing I'm gonna do is film that trick.
cues.zh: 我满脑子想的都是，哥们，等我醒来、好起来，我要做的第一件事就是去拍那个动作。

cues.en: And indeed, I did. It was the very first thing I filmed, which was
cues.zh: 结果我真的做到了。那是我拍的第一个动作，真是太

cues.en: awesome.
cues.zh: 棒了。

cues.en: Now let me... I told you a little bit about the evolution of the tricks. Consider that content in a sense. What we do as street skaters is
cues.zh: 现在让我……我刚才简单讲了讲这些技巧的演变。从某种意义上说，你可以把这看作是内容。我们作为街头滑板手，

cues.en: you have these tricks. Say I'm working on dark slides or a primo. Did you guys know this stuff now?
cues.zh: 你会做这些技巧。比方说我在练暗滑（dark slide）或是普里莫停（primo）。你们现在知道这些东西吗？

cues.en: What you do is you cruise around the same streets that you've seen a 100 times.
cues.zh: 你要做的是在同一条你见过上百次的街道上四处滑行。

cues.en: But suddenly, because you already have something in this fixed domain
cues.zh: 但突然之间，因为你的这个固定领域里

cues.en: of this target, it's like, what will match this trick? How can I expand?
cues.zh: 已经有了这样一个目标，就会觉得：什么样的新招能跟这个配合？我该如何拓展？

cues.en: How can the context, how can the environment change the very nature of what I do? So you drive and drive and drive. And,
cues.zh: 上下文和环境又将如何改变我所做之事的本质？所以你一遍又一遍地滑着。而且，

cues.en: actually, I gotta admit this because I I was struggling with this because I'm here. But I'll just say it is I cannot tell you not only to be here in front of you, but what a privilege it is to be at USC campus because I have been escorted off of this campus so many times. So
cues.zh: 说实话，我得承认这一点，因为我一直为此感到纠结，毕竟我人就在这。但我还是要说，站在这里面对着大家，不仅如此，能来到南加州大学（USC）的校园是何等的荣幸，因为我以前曾无数次被保安从这个校园里驱逐出去。所以

cues.en: let me give you another example of how context shapes
cues.zh: 让我再举一个例子，说说环境是如何塑造

cues.en: content.
cues.zh: 内容的。

cues.en: This is a place not that far from here. It's a rotten neighborhood. Your first consideration is am I gonna get beat up? You go out and there... See this wall?
cues.zh: 这是一个离这儿不远的地方。那是个治安很乱的街区。你首先考虑的是：我会不会挨揍？你走出去，然后那里……看到这面墙了吗？

cues.en: It's fairly mellow, and it's
cues.zh: 它相当温和，而且它在

cues.en: beckoning
cues.zh: 召唤着

cues.en: to do bank tricks. Right? But there's this other aspect of it that that... For wheelies. So check this out.
cues.zh: 你去做斜坡技巧。对吧？但它还有另一个方面……为了玩滑行。所以来看看这个。

cues.en: There's a few tricks. Again, how environment changes the nature of your tricks. Freestyle oriented,
cues.zh: 还有一些别的技巧。同样，环境是如何改变你的技巧本质的。偏向自由式，

cues.en: manual down, wheelie down. Watch this one. Oh, I love this. It's like surfing, this one, the way you catch it.
cues.zh: 前轮滑下去，滑行下去。看这个。哦，我太喜欢这个了。这个感觉就像冲浪一样，你抓住板的那个样子。

cues.en: This one,
cues.zh: 这一个，

cues.en: a little sketchy going backwards. And watch the back foot. Watch the back foot.
cues.zh: 往回看有点勉强。注意后脚。注意后脚。

cues.en: Mental
cues.zh: 心理

cues.en: note right there. Again, we'll get back to that.
cues.zh: 记一下。这个我们回头再讲。

cues.en: Here, back flip, back flip.
cues.zh: 这里，后空翻，后空翻。

cues.en: Okay. Up there, that was called a three sixty flip. Notice how the board flipped and spun this way, both axes.
cues.zh: 好。刚才那个叫三百六十度翻转。注意板是怎么翻转并朝这个方向旋转的，两个轴都动了。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 还有

cues.en: another example of how the context changed and the creative process
cues.zh: 另一个例子，说明情境如何改变，以及创作过程

cues.en: for me and for most skaters
cues.zh: 对我来说，对大多数滑手来说

cues.en: is you go, you get out of the car, you check for security, you check for stuff.
cues.zh: 就是你下车，查看安保情况，检查周围环境。

cues.en: It's funny. You get to know their rhythm. Do you know all the guys that cruise around?
cues.zh: 挺有意思的。你会熟悉他们的节奏。那些四处巡逻的人你都认识吗？

cues.en: Skateboarding is such a humbling thing, man. No matter how good you are, right, you still gotta deal with... And so you hit this wall.
cues.zh: 滑板就是这么让人谦卑，哥们。不管你多厉害，对吧，你还是得面对……然后你就撞上这堵墙。

cues.en: And when I hit it, the first thing you do is you fall forward.
cues.zh: 当我撞上时，第一反应就是向前摔。

cues.en: I'm like, alright. Alright. As you adjust as you adjust,
cues.zh: 我心想，好吧。好吧。你一边调整一边调整，

cues.en: you punch it up. And then when I would do that, it was throwing my shoulder this way,
cues.zh: 你加大力度。然后我这么做的时候，肩膀会往这边甩，

cues.en: which as I was doing, was like, oh, wow. That's begging for a three sixty flip because that's how you load up for a three sixty flip.
cues.zh: 我一边做一边想，哦哇。这简直就是在为三百六十度翻转做准备，因为那就是你为三百六十度翻转蓄力的方式。

cues.en: And so this is what I wanna emphasize that as you can imagine,
cues.zh: 所以这就是我想强调的，你可以想象，

cues.en: all of these tricks are made of
cues.zh: 所有这些动作都是由

cues.en: sub movements, executive motor functions, more granular to the degree to which I can't quite tell you. But one thing I do know is every trick is made of combining two or three or four or five movements.
cues.zh: 子动作组成的，执行性运动功能，精细到我都没法完全说清。但有一点我确定，每个动作都是由两三个、四个或五个动作组合而成的。

cues.en: And so as I'm going up, these things are floating around, and you have to sort of let the cognitive mind, like, rest back, pull it back a little bit, and let your intuition go as you feel these things.
cues.zh: 所以当我往上滑时，脑子里会浮现各种动作碎片，你得收敛一下理性思维，稍微退一步，跟着感觉让直觉带路。

cues.en: And these these sub movements are just kind of floating around, and as the wall hits you, they connect themselves to an extent. And that's when cognitive mind think, oh, three sixty flip, I'm gonna make that. So that's how that works for me, the creative process, the process itself of street skating.
cues.zh: 这些微小的动作组合在脑海中浮动，当墙面迎面扑来时，它们自然而然地连贯起来。这时理性思维才会冒出来：“哦，360 flip，我要做这个。”对我来说，创作过程就是这样，街式滑板本身也是这个过程。

cues.en: So next... Oh, mind you,
cues.zh: 接下来……哦，顺便提一句，

cues.en: those are the community. These are some of the best skaters in the world.
cues.zh: 这就是那个滑板圈子。他们是世界上最顶尖的一批滑手。

cues.en: See these are my friends. Oh my gosh. They're such good people.
cues.zh: 看，这些都是我的朋友。天哪，他们人真的太好了。

cues.en: And the beauty of skateboarding is that no one guy is the best. In fact, I know this is rotten to say, they're my friends,
cues.zh: 滑板的魅力就在于没有人是绝对的第一。其实，虽然这么说有点损，毕竟他们是我的朋友，

cues.en: but a couple of them actually don't look that that comfortable on the board. What makes them great
cues.zh: 但其中有几位在板上看起来其实没那么自如。而让他们非凡出众的，

cues.en: is the degree to which they use their skateboarding to individuate themselves. Every single one of these guys, you look at them, you could see a silhouette of them, and you realize, like, oh, that's him. That's Haslam. That's Costin. There's these guys. These are the guys.
cues.zh: 是他们通过滑板展现自身独特风格的程度。这里面的每一个人，你只要看一眼剪影就能认出来：“哦，那是他，那是 Haslam，那是 Costin。”就是这群人，就是他们。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: skaters,
cues.zh: 滑手们，

cues.en: I think they tend to be outsiders
cues.zh: 我觉得他们往往是一群局外人，

cues.en: who seek a sense of belonging,
cues.zh: 渴望寻找归属感，

cues.en: but belonging on their own terms.
cues.zh: 但必须按他们自己的方式去获得归属。

cues.en: And real respect is given by how much we take what other guys do, these basic tricks, three sixty flips.
cues.zh: 而真正的尊重，在于我们在多大程度上借鉴别人的招式——比如这些基础动作、360 flip。

cues.en: We take that, we make it our own,
cues.zh: 我们吸收它，化为己有，

cues.en: and then we contribute back to the community in a way that edifies the community itself.
cues.zh: 然后回馈社区，让社区本身得到提升。

cues.en: The greater the contribution,
cues.zh: 贡献越大，

cues.en: the more we express and form our individuality,
cues.zh: 我们就越能表达和塑造自己的个性，

cues.en: which is so important to a lot of us who feel like rejects to begin with.
cues.zh: 这对我们很多人来说非常重要，尤其是那些一开始就觉得自己被排斥的人。

cues.en: The summation of that
cues.zh: 这一切的累积

cues.en: gives us something we could never achieve as an individual.
cues.zh: 带给我们作为个体永远无法企及的成就。

cues.en: I should say this, there's some sort of beautiful symmetry
cues.zh: 我得说，这里有种美妙的对称

cues.en: that the degree to which we connect to a community is in proportion to our individuality,
cues.zh: 我们与社区的连接程度，与我们的个性成正比，

cues.en: which we are expressing by what we do.
cues.zh: 而我们正是通过所做之事来表达这种个性。

cues.en: Next,
cues.zh: 接下来，

cues.en: these guys, very similar community that's extremely conducive to innovation.
cues.zh: 这些人，非常相似的社区，极其有利于创新。

cues.en: Notice a couple of these shots
cues.zh: 注意其中几个镜头

cues.en: from the police department.
cues.zh: 来自警察部门。

cues.en: But it is quite similar. I mean, what is it to hack? Right? It's knowing a technology so well that you can manipulate it and steer it to do things it was never intended to do. Right? And they're not all bad. You can be a Linux kernel hacker, make it more stable.
cues.zh: 但非常相似。我是说，什么叫黑客？对吧？就是把一门技术掌握得如此透彻，以至于你能操纵它、引导它去做它本不该做的事。对吧？而且他们并不都是坏人。你可以做Linux内核黑客，让它更稳定。

cues.en: Right? More safe, more secure. You can be an iOS hacker,
cues.zh: 对吧？更安全、更可靠。你可以做iOS黑客，

cues.en: Make your iPhone do stuff it wasn't supposed to.
cues.zh: 让你的iPhone做它本不该做的事。

cues.en: Not authorized, but not illegal.
cues.zh: 未经授权，但并不违法。

cues.en: And then you've got some of these guys. Right? What they do is very similar to our creative process. They connect disparate information,
cues.zh: 然后还有这些人。对吧？他们所做的和我们的创造过程非常相似。他们连接不同的信息，

cues.en: and they bring it together in a way
cues.zh: 并以一种

cues.en: that security analyst doesn't expect. Right? Doesn't make them good people,
cues.zh: 安全分析师意想不到的方式把它们整合起来。对吧？这并不让他们成为好人，

cues.en: but it's at the heart of engineering. It's the heart of a creative community, an innovative community.
cues.zh: 但这是工程的核心。这是创意社区、创新社区的核心。

cues.en: And the open source community, the basic ethos of it is take what other people do,
cues.zh: 开源社区的基本精神就是吸收别人的成果，

cues.en: make it better, give it back so we all rise further. Very similar communities. Very similar.
cues.zh: 把它做得更好，再回馈回去，这样大家都能共同进步。这两个群体非常相似，非常相似。

cues.en: We have our edgier size too.
cues.zh: 我们也有锋芒毕露的一面。

cues.en: It's funny. My dad was right. These are my peers.
cues.zh: 挺有意思的。我爸说得对，这些人都是我的同侪。

cues.en: But I respect what they do, and they respect what I do because they can do things...
cues.zh: 但我很敬佩他们的所作所为，他们也尊重我的工作，因为他们能做到……

cues.en: It's amazing what they can do. In fact, one of them,
cues.zh: 他们能做的事简直不可思议。事实上，他们当中有个人，

cues.en: he was Ernst and Young's
cues.zh: 曾获评安永（Ernst & Young）

cues.en: entrepreneur of the year for San Diego County. So they're not. You never know who you're dealing with. We've
cues.zh: 圣迭戈县的年度企业家。所以他们可不简单，你永远不知道自己面对的是何方神圣。我们

cues.en: all had some degree of fame. In fact, I've I've been... I have had so much success that I...
cues.zh: 都曾小有名气。事实上，我……我也取得过很多成功，以至于我……

cues.en: Strangely, I always feel unworthy of. I I... I've had a patent, that was cool, and we started a company. It grew, and it became the biggest,
cues.zh: 很奇怪，我总觉得自己受之有愧。我拿到过专利，这很酷，后来我们创立了一家公司。它不断壮大，做到了行业第一，

cues.en: And then it went down, and then it became the biggest again, which is harder than the first time. And then we sold it, and then we sold it again.
cues.zh: 后来跌入低谷，接着又重回巅峰，这比第一次登顶还要难。再后来我们把它卖了，之后又转手卖了一次。

cues.en: So I've had some success.
cues.zh: 所以我也算小有成就。

cues.en: And in the end, when you've had all of these things, what is it that continues to drive you? As I mentioned, the knee stuff and these things, what is it that will punch you? Because it's not just the mind. What is it that will punch you and make you do something
cues.zh: 可走到最后，当你拥有了这一切，到底是什么在持续驱动你前行？就像我之前提到膝盖受伤那些事，是什么在重重敲打你？因为这不仅仅关乎心智。究竟是什么在猛击你、促使你行动，

cues.en: and bring it to another level? And when you've had it all, sometimes, guys, they they die on the vine with all of that talent.
cues.zh: 并把它提升到全新高度？当你拥有一切时，有时候，有些人就会空有一身天赋却在半途荒废掉。

cues.en: And one of the things we've had, all of us, is fame. I think the best kind of fame because you can take it off. I've been all around the world,
cues.zh: 我们所有人都有的一样东西，就是名气。我觉得这是最好的一种名气，因为你可以把它卸下来。我走遍世界各地，

cues.en: and there'll be a thousand kids crying out your name, and it's such a weird visceral experience. It's like it's disorienting.
cues.zh: 会有上千个孩子喊着你的名字，那是一种非常怪异又直击感官的体验。让人晕头转向。

cues.en: And you get in a car and you drive away.
cues.zh: 然后你上车，开走。

cues.en: And ten minute drive, and you get out, and no one gives a rat who you are.
cues.zh: 开十分钟车，你下车，没人管你是谁。

cues.en: And it gives you that clarity of perspective of, man, I'm just me. And popularity,
cues.zh: 它让你清楚地看到：老兄，我就是我自己。而受欢迎程度，

cues.en: what does that really mean again? Not much.
cues.zh: 那到底又意味着什么？没什么。

cues.en: It's pure respect that drives us. That's the one thing that makes us do what we do. I've had over a dozen bones. These guys... This guy over, what, eight, 10 concussions to the point where it's comedy. Right?
cues.zh: 是纯粹的尊重在驱动我们。这是唯一让我们去做我们所作所为的东西。我断过十几根骨头。这些家伙……这位老兄，得有八次、十次脑震荡，都到了搞笑的程度。对吧？

cues.en: It
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: is actually comedy. They mess with him.
cues.zh: 其实真成喜剧了。他们拿他开涮。

cues.en: Next.
cues.zh: 下一个。

cues.en: And this is something deeper, and this is where I'm...
cues.zh: 而这是更深层的东西，也是我……

cues.en: I think I was on tour when I I I was reading one of the Feynman biographies. It was the red one or the blue one.
cues.zh: 我想我当时在巡演，我我我在读一本 Feynman 传记。是红色那本还是蓝色那本来着。

cues.en: And he made this he made this statement that was so profound to me.
cues.zh: 他讲过一句话，这句话对我来说太深刻了。

cues.en: It was that the the Nobel Prize was the tombstone on all great work.
cues.zh: 他说，诺贝尔奖是所有伟大工作的墓碑。

cues.en: And it resonated because I had won 35 out of 36 contests that I'd entered over eleven years, and it made me bananas.
cues.zh: 这话引起共鸣，因为十一年里我参加了36场比赛，赢了35场，这让我快疯了。

cues.en: In fact, winning isn't the word I won at once. The rest of time, you're just defending, and you get into this, like, turtle posture, you know, where you're not doing it. It usurped the joy of what I love to do because I was no longer doing it to create and have fun.
cues.zh: 其实，“赢”这个词不准确。我只赢过一次。其余时间，你只是在防守，你会进入一种像乌龟一样的姿态，你知道，就是你并没有真正在做那件事。它夺走了我做热爱之事的快乐，因为我不再是为了创造和享受乐趣而做。

cues.en: And when it died out from under me, that was one of the most liberating things because I could create.
cues.zh: 当它从我脚下消失时，那反而是最解放的事情之一，因为我可以去创造。

cues.en: And look, I understand that I am
cues.zh: 你看，我明白我

cues.en: on the very edge of preachy right here. I'm not here to do that. It's just that I'm in front of a very privileged audience. If you guys aren't already leaders in your community,
cues.zh: 现在有点说教的味道了。我不是来干这个的。只是我面对着一群非常幸运的听众。如果你们还不是社区里的领袖，

cues.en: you probably will be.
cues.zh: 那你们很可能将来会是。

cues.en: And if there's anything I can give you that will transcend what I've gotten from skateboarding,
cues.zh: 如果我能给你们什么，能超越我从滑板中获得的东西，

cues.en: the only things of of meaning, I think, in a permanence... It's not fame. It's not popular. It's all these things. It's what it is,
cues.zh: 我认为，唯一有意义、能持久的东西……不是名声。不是受欢迎。不是这些东西。事实是，

cues.en: Is that there's an intrinsic value in creating something for the sake of creating it.
cues.zh: 就是为创造而创造某样东西，这本身就有内在价值。

cues.en: And better than that, because, man, I'm 46 year old... Or I'll be 46, and how pathetic is that that I'm still skateboarding? But there is there is this beauty
cues.zh: 比这更好的是，因为，天哪，我46岁了……或者说我快46了，还在滑板，多可悲啊？但这里面有一种美，

cues.en: in dropping
cues.zh: 就是把它

cues.en: it into a community of your own making
cues.zh: 投入你自己打造的社区

cues.en: and seeing it dispersed
cues.zh: 看着它扩散开来

cues.en: and seeing younger, more talented, just different talent. Take it to levels you can never imagine because that lives on.
cues.zh: 看着更年轻、更有才华、不同类型的人才，把它带到你无法想象的高度，因为那会延续下去。

cues.en: So thank you for your time.
cues.zh: 所以，谢谢大家的时间。

cues.en: I have a question for you.
cues.zh: 我有个问题问你。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: you really reinvented yourself in the past from freestyle to street. And I think it was about four years ago you officially retired.
cues.zh: 你过去确实重塑了自己，从自由式到街头。我记得大约四年前你正式退役了。

cues.en: Is that it? What's
cues.zh: 就这样吗？接下来

cues.en: next?
cues.zh: 是什么？

cues.en: That's a good question. Something tells me it's not the end. Yeah. I I I I...
cues.zh: 这是个好问题。我有种感觉，这不是终点。是啊。我我我我……

cues.en: Every time you think you've chased something down, it's funny. No matter how good you are, and I know guys like this, it feels like you're polishing a turd. You know?
cues.zh: 每次你以为自己追到了什么，很有意思。不管你多厉害，我认识这样的人，感觉就像你在打磨一坨屎。你知道吗？

cues.en: And that's...
cues.zh: 而这……

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: I thought the only way I can extend this is is to change something infrastructural.
cues.zh: 我原以为唯一能扩展它的办法，就是改动一些基础设施层面的东西。

cues.en: And so that's what I proceeded to do through a long story, one of desperation.
cues.zh: 于是我就这么做了，经历了一段漫长的、充满绝望的过程。

cues.en: Mhmm. So
cues.zh: 嗯。所以

cues.en: if I do it rather than talk about it, if I do it Alright. You'll be the first to know. Anymore. You'll get a text.
cues.zh: 如果我是直接做，而不是光谈——如果我直接做。行。你会是第一个知道的。不再多说了。会给你发消息。

cues.en: Alright. Thank you.
cues.zh: 好。谢谢。

cues.en: Good day.
cues.zh: 再见。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。
